title: GraphQL Endpoint Review
summary: The request or response looks like GraphQL traffic and should be reviewed for schema exposure, field-level authorization, and method/content-type weaknesses.
operator_questions: Does this GraphQL endpoint accept GET or form-urlencoded requests in addition to the expected POST JSON flow?
Can you confirm whether introspection, aliases, or object ID arguments change the authorization surface for this endpoint?

title: Mass Assignment / Auto-Binding Review
summary: The JSON body includes privilege-related fields and should be checked for silent acceptance of server-managed properties.
operator_questions: Are fields like role, admin, permissions, price, balance, or status meant to be server-controlled for this operation?
Does the server ignore, normalize, or persist these sensitive JSON fields when you replay the same request?

title: Path Traversal / File Retrieval Review
summary: File or path-style inputs suggest reviewing filename normalization and arbitrary file access boundaries.
operator_questions: Does the endpoint read local files, templates, exports, or generated documents based on client-supplied path values?
Do simple path normalization changes alter whether the server rejects, normalizes, or retrieves content?

title: HTTP Request Smuggling Review
summary: Conflicting request-length framing or chunked transfer hints should be reviewed for front-end versus back-end parsing differences.
operator_questions: Does this request pass through a proxy, load balancer, CDN, or other front-end component before it reaches the application?
Can you confirm whether a one-header framing change causes a front-end versus back-end response mismatch without broad fuzzing?

title: Unsafe Deserialization Review
summary: Serialized-object style markers suggest the endpoint may deserialize structured client input and should be reviewed for parser and integrity risks.
operator_questions: Is this opaque blob or serialized structure expected to be generated and validated by the server rather than trusted from the client?
Do small structural changes trigger parser, type, or integrity-check errors that suggest server-side deserialization?

title: Server-Side Template Injection Review
summary: Template-like inputs on rendering, preview, or email-style routes should be reviewed for server-side evaluation of user-controlled expressions.
operator_questions: Does this route render server-side templates, generated emails, previews, or invoices using user-controlled fields?
Do simple expression-style markers evaluate, escape differently, or trigger template-engine specific errors?

title: Secret Exposure Review
summary: The response body appears to contain keys, tokens, or private material markers that should not be exposed to the client.
operator_questions: Does the response include API keys, private key blocks, debug secrets, or environment data that should remain server-side?
Can you confirm whether the same exposure appears only on this route or across related debug, config, or error responses?

title: Cryptographic Failures Review
summary: Transport or cookie protection signals suggest reviewing whether sensitive data is exposed without expected cryptographic safeguards.
operator_questions: Is this sensitive route reachable over plain HTTP or with cookies that are usable without the Secure flag?
Do you see missing transport protections, weak key material handling, or other cryptographic control gaps around this flow?

title: Race Condition Review
summary: State-changing workflow requests should be reviewed for parallel execution windows and duplicate processing.
operator_questions: Does this endpoint enforce one-time use, rate limits, balances, or state transitions that could be affected by parallel requests?
Can you reproduce a behavioral difference by replaying the same state-changing request in parallel Repeater tabs?

title: Insecure Design / Workflow Guardrail Review
summary: Security-critical workflows with client-controlled state or sequencing assumptions should be reviewed for missing server-side guardrails.
operator_questions: Does this flow rely on client-visible sequencing, state, amount, or approval fields that should be enforced only on the server side?
Can you identify one skipped, replayed, or reordered step that still completes without the expected business control?
